chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to me from Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed, who reported from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Khaqan al-Nahdi, who reported from Sulaim, the servant at Darb al-Hubb, from Ibrahim ibn Uqbah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Nadhr ibn Qarwash al-Nahdi, the camel hirer at Kufa, that Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, said:

"Indeed, the religious person reflects and serenity befalls him; he submits and becomes humble; he is content and becomes self-sufficient; he is pleased with what he has been given; he is alone and needs no company; he abandons base desires and becomes free; he divests himself of the world and is protected from evils; he casts aside jealousy and love appears; he does not threaten people, so they do not threaten him; he does not sin against them, so he is safe from them; his soul is generous about everything, so he succeeds and reaches perfection in virtue; and he perceives well-being, so he is safe from regret."

key_terms.السكينة: Serenity; inner tranquility that descends upon the faithful
key_terms.الشهوات: Base desires; worldly lusts and passions
key_terms.المحبة: Love; genuine affection that results from absence of jealousy
key_terms.صاحب الدين: A person of religion; one who genuinely adheres to religious life

ai.seo_question: What are the traits and outcomes of a truly religious person according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) describes the qualities and outcomes of a truly religious person through a series of paired actions and spiritual results, showing how inner discipline leads to freedom, love, safety, and ultimate freedom from regret. This teaching was delivered in the scholarly gatherings of Shaykh al-Mufid in 10th-century Baghdad.
